sn22.86:1.1: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.
sn22.86:1.2: Now on that occasion the Venerable Anurādha was dwelling in a forest hut not far from the Blessed One.
sn22.86:1.3: Then a number of wanderers of other sects approached the Venerable Anurādha and exchanged greetings with him.
sn22.86:1.4: When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, they sat down to one side and said to him:
sn22.86:1.5: “Friend Anurādha, when a Tathāgata is describing a Tathāgata — the highest type of person, the supreme person, the attainer of the supreme attainment — he describes him in terms of these four cases:
sn22.86:1.6: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”
sn22.86:2.1: When this was said, the Venerable Anurādha said to those wanderers:
sn22.86:2.2: ‘Friends, when a Tathāgata is describing a Tathāgata — the highest type of person, the supreme person, the attainer of the supreme attainment — he describes him apart from these four cases:
sn22.86:2.3: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death.’”
sn22.86:2.4: When this was said, those wanderers said to the Venerable Anurādha:
sn22.86:2.5: ‘This bhikkhu must be newly ordained, not long gone forth; or, if he is an elder, he must be an incompetent fool.”
sn22.86:2.6: Then those wanderers of other sects, having denigrated the Venerable Anurādha with the terms “newly ordained” and “fool,” rose from their seats and departed.
sn22.86:3.1: Then, not long after those wanderers had left, it occurred to the Venerable Anurādha:
sn22.86:3.2: “If those wanderers of other sects should question me further,
sn22.86:3.3: how should I answer if I am to state what has been said by the Blessed One and not misrepresent him with what is contrary to fact? And how should I explain in accordance with the Dhamma, so that no reasonable consequence of my assertion would give ground for criticism?”
sn22.86:4.1: Then the Venerable Anurādha approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and reported to the Blessed One everything that had happened, asking:
sn22.86:6.1: “If those wanderers of other sects should question me further,
sn22.86:6.3: so that no reasonable consequence of my assertion would give ground for criticism?”
sn22.86:7.16: He understands: ‘… there is no more for this state of being.’
sn22.86:8.2: do you regard form as the Tathāgata?”
sn22.86:9.2: do you regard the Tathāgata as in form?”
sn22.86:9.4: – “Do you regard the Tathāgata as apart from form?”
sn22.86:9.6: – “Do you regard the Tathāgata as in feeling?
sn22.86:10.2: do you regard form, feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness [taken together] as the Tathāgata?”
sn22.86:11.2: do you regard the Tathāgata as one who is without form, without feeling, without perception, without volitional formations, without consciousness?”
sn22.86:12.1: “But, Anurādha, when the Tathāgata is not apprehended by you as real and actual here in this very life, is it fitting for you to declare:
sn22.86:12.2: ‘Friends, when a Tathāgata is describing a Tathāgata — the highest type of person, the supreme person, the attainer of the supreme attainment — he describes him apart from these four cases:
sn22.86:12.3: ‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ or … ‘The Tathāgata neither exists nor does not exist after death’?”
sn22.86:13.2: Formerly, Anurādha, and also now, I make known just suffering and the cessation of suffering.”
